correctness.rationale: Simultaneous permutations of paired indices and class exchange preserve cost and decrease the centered operator norm under averaging. Invariant chains have cost n[(n-1)a+t b], since each cross-edge is counted once. Writing s=(n-1)a+b, block splitting gives the nontrivial eigenvalues 1-2s, 1-na and 1+na-2s. For r=1-theta, feasibility implies a>=r/n and (r+na)/2<=s<=(1+theta)/2, hence a<=2 theta/n and b>=max(0,[r-(n-2)a]/2). The lower cost envelope has slopes (n-1)-t(n-2)/2 and n-1 after the kink. Its selected points are feasible: the equal-weight point has nontrivial eigenvalues 2 theta-1, theta, theta; the cap point a=2 theta/n has -theta, 1-2 theta, theta; at b=0, a=r/(n-2), the spectral inequalities hold at and above theta_c and s<1. Convexity supplies the full feasible optimal tie segment, and positive t makes equality in the lower bound necessary. For theta<1/3 the necessary interval is empty. With b=0 feasibility requires theta>=theta_c; averaging transfers the exclusion to arbitrary symmetric competitors. The costs are continuous and strictly decrease to the 1/3 floor; their affine inverses give the stated budget branches, and B=0 forces the identity. The proof also covers theta=1/3 and theta=theta_c; the list of all minimizers is only for the invariant class.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For t>t_c write C_t=C_{t_c}+n(t-t_c)b. Both lower bounds are simultaneously tight: the capacity optimizer above gives equality below theta_c, and the crown endpoint of the scaled continuous-time face is feasible at and above theta_c, giving equality there. Equality fixes both a and b. For t<t_c scaling the unique continuous-time equal-weight optimizer attains its gap-derived lower bound without violating SLEM. At t=t_c the continuous-time equality face is clipped by the bipartition constraint a<=2 theta/n; the other nontrivial eigenvalues there are theta and 1-na and cause no extra cut. This also gives the forced matching-weight claim by averaging, the 1/3 floor from the capacity minimum, and the budget version by inversion. No new independent optimization or residual theorem is needed.
